title: Macrophage ILF3 promotes abdominal aortic aneurysm by inducing inflammatory imbalance in male mice

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, descriptions of the ILF3 macrophage-overexpression and macrophage-knockout mouse strains (Figs. 2 and 3)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper assigns exactly the same genotype to opposite manipulations: the overexpression strain is stated to be "ILF3^flox/floxLysMCre^+" (ILF3^M-Tg), while the knockout strain is also stated to be "ILF3^flox/floxLysMCre^+" (ILF3^M-KO). Likewise, both respective controls are described as ILF3^flox/floxLysMCre^−. A single stated genotype cannot simultaneously be a Cre-mediated conditional knockout of a floxed endogenous allele and a conditional overexpression line. If one line instead contains a floxed-stop transgene, that distinct allele must be identified. As written, the central gain- and loss-of-function experiments are not reproducibly or logically described.

The reported direction of IL-10 change in ILF3-deficient mice is contradictory. The in-vitro paragraph says that ILF3-deficient macrophages had reduced MCP-1, IL-6 and TNF-alpha but that "IL-10 levels were ... intensified due to the lack of ILF3." In contrast, the immediately following in-vivo paragraph says MCP-1, IL-6, TNF-alpha, "and IL-10 exhibited a pronounced decrement in the ILF3^M-KO" mice, and says all were significantly upregulated in ILF3^M-Tg mice. It then states that IL-10 was "diametrically opposed" to the pro-inflammatory mediators. These cannot all be true; the figures or text must be corrected to give a single, explicit IL-10 direction for each model.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, Fig. 5 mechanistic interpretation of Keap1-Nrf2 signaling
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The manuscript gives mutually incompatible interpretations of the Nrf2 result. It reports reduced Keap1, increased Nrf2 nuclear translocation/ARE DNA binding, and later summarizes this as "activating Keap1-Nrf2 pathway due to reduced Keap1 expression." However, the preceding conclusion says ILF3 deficiency modulates balance by "simultaneously inhibiting the NF-kB and Keap1-Nrf2 signaling pathways." Reduced Keap1 with increased Nrf2 nuclear/ARE activity is activation of the Nrf2 arm, not inhibition of the Keap1-Nrf2 pathway. The mechanistic conclusion therefore reverses its own stated result.

predicted_errors.error_location: Throughout the in-vivo AAA experiments described as macrophage-specific ILF3 manipulation
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The study repeatedly calls LysM-Cre-mediated manipulation "macrophage" ILF3 deficiency or overexpression and attributes the in-vivo AAA phenotype specifically to macrophages. LysM-Cre is not macrophage-specific: it recombines efficiently in neutrophils and monocytes and can recombine in other myeloid populations. Thus, the Ang-II and CaCl2 in-vivo phenotypes cannot be assigned specifically to macrophage ILF3 from these mice alone. Macrophage culture experiments may show macrophage-intrinsic effects, but they do not exclude a contribution from other LysM-positive cells to the AAA phenotype. The model and the corresponding causal claims need to be relabeled as myeloid-cell targeted or supported with macrophage-specific validation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Fig. 1B-C caption and Results paragraph describing GEO2R differential-expression analysis
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Results state that the human and mouse DEGs/heatmaps in Fig. 1B-C were obtained through "GEO2R analysis," whereas the Fig. 1 caption says that comparisons in "1B-1C" used a two-tailed Student's t-test. GEO2R's standard differential-expression workflow uses limma moderated t-statistics, not ordinary Student's t-tests. The paper therefore reports an incompatible statistical procedure for these panels. It should state the actual GEO2R/limma model, its multiple-testing treatment, and the precise thresholds used.
